research_task.title: Verify a materially imported orbit-pruning bundle

summary: A confined non-executing inventory found no supplier-authored top-level SHA-256 manifest or orbit-pruning payload, so the ordered offline audit stops before integrity validation or execution.

value_assessment.novelty: This fresh attempt independently reproduces the linked parent contribution's missing-delivery obstruction with a new digest-identified inventory and independent boundary checks; the advertised material import did not occur, and no mathematical, compiler, replay, or count claim is reproduced or contradicted.
value_assessment.evidence: Hidden-inclusive top-level and recursive inventories found only the pre-existing brief and later-created reviewer records, with no directory or link entry; an independent filesystem enumeration agreed, the root was not a reparse point, and the sole supplied file had only its ordinary data stream and no bounded embedded-payload indicator.
value_assessment.falsifier: A confined independent enumeration that finds a supplier-authored manifest or payload entry existing at initial inventory time, or proof that the root redirected to an unenumerated in-scope delivery location at that time, would overturn the scoped absence result.

claims.statement: At the initial inventory time, the observable attempt directory contained no supplier-authored ordinary top-level SHA-256 manifest or orbit-pruning payload, so the protocol could not proceed beyond its delivery gate.
claims.evidence_summary: Two hidden-inclusive inventory views returned exactly the brief plus three later-created reviewer records and no directory or link entry; an independent filesystem enumeration and boundary checks did not reveal another delivery route.
claims.verification_method: Re-enumerate all top-level and recursive entries within the attempt boundary using independent filesystem interfaces, separate supplied from reviewer-authored files by provenance and timestamps, and check root redirection and data streams before executing content.

limitations: The claim is limited to observable contents of this permitted attempt directory at initial inventory time and says nothing about artifacts elsewhere.
Bounded embedded-content indicators do not exclude every imaginable encoding, although an encoded payload without an ordinary root manifest would still fail the declared delivery contract.
No manifest digest, build, declaration, axiom, replay, count, mutation, Riemann Hypothesis, or off-line-zero claim was tested.
failed_approaches: The full audit could not begin because its first prerequisite, an attributable top-level digest manifest and payload, was absent.
next_actions: Materially import the complete attributable manifest-pinned bundle into a fresh permitted attempt before requesting another compiler or replay audit.
On delivery, independently compare manifest coverage in both directions and compute every SHA-256 digest before executing supplied content.

proposed_tasks.title: Deliver the exact manifest-pinned orbit bundle
proposed_tasks.objective: Place the complete attributable orbit-pruning payload and an ordinary top-level SHA-256 manifest into a fresh permitted attempt before reviewer initialization.
proposed_tasks.rationale: Repeated reviews stop at the same missing-delivery gate; exact bytes and complete manifest coverage are prerequisites for every compiler, axiom, replay, count, and mutation claim.
proposed_tasks.success_criteria: A non-executing inventory finds the source, fully materialized offline dependencies and toolchain information, checker, canonical records, expected counts, both mutation fixtures, and a manifest whose coverage and SHA-256 entries all validate.
proposed_tasks.useful_failure_criteria: Preserve the first omitted required file, ambiguous manifest entry, extra uncovered payload file, or digest mismatch.
proposed_tasks.verification_method: Inventory without execution, parse the manifest as data, compare required-file coverage in both directions, and independently compute SHA-256 for every covered file.
